title: Buy-committee evidence and competitive appendix
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document is a concise evidence pack for buyer committees (procurement, security, platform engineering, and product leadership) when evaluating Redwood Inference. It pairs a short competitive appendix with clear decision artifacts (SLOs, benchmark snippets, pricing scenarios, and a security FAQ) that field teams can attach to an executive pitch or include in an RFP response.

Audience: Sales engineers, account executives, customer success managers, and sales leadership preparing for buy-committee reviews.

Executive summary

- What Redwood solves: predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with production-grade observability and controls.
- Core buyer outcomes: reduced per-token cost by up to 3x vs unmanaged GPU hosting (typical), 99.95% availability for Dedicated customers, and a single API/operational model across environments.
- Primary differentiators: unifed runtime with workload-aware batching, routing policies, and rollouts; first-class observability at token-level; and private deployment options with KMS/HSM integrations.

Positioning statements (by buyer persona)

- Platform engineering: "Ship LLM features without bespoke serving stacks — same API from dev to on-prem, with per-route SLOs and automatic fallbacks."
- Security/compliance: "Private control plane option with audit logging, VPC peering, and HSM-backed key management for regulated workloads."
- Product/Revenue: "Faster time to market with predictable economics — pilot to scale with canary rollouts, cost controls, and model version pinning."

Competitive appendix (quick read)

Table: feature vs. competitor matrix (excerpt)

| Feature | Redwood Inference | Major Cloud ML Endpoint | Inference Vendor X | Open self-host |
|--------|-------------------|------------------------|--------------------|----------------|
| Unified API (hosted/dedicated/private) | Yes | Limited | Yes (but ops heavy) | No (custom) |
| Token-level cost breakdowns | Yes | No | Partial | No |
| Private control plane + HSM | Yes | Limited | Optional | Varies |
| Intelligent batching + KV caching | Yes | Partial | Partial | No |
| SLA-backed Dedicated | Yes (99.95%) | Optional | Optional | No |
| Built-in rollouts & automatic fallback | Yes | No | Partial | No |

Short competitor notes:

- Major Cloud ML Endpoint: strong for general-purpose managed hosting and wide ecosystem; weaker on per-token economics, model rollouts, and private control plane.
- Inference Vendor X: competitive on optimized runtimes but often requires more professional services and custom ops for equivalent privacy controls.
- Open self-host: cheapest at scale for some shops but lacks observability, routing, and fast rollouts without significant engineering investment.

Typical objections and rebuttals

1) "We can self-host for cheaper."
   - Rebuttal: Total cost includes engineering time, versioning/rollout complexity, and the absence of smart batching and KV caching that materially lower token cost; Redwood’s Optimize toolkit and recommendations often reduce operator burden and lower overall TCO.

2) "Vendor lock-in concerns."
   - Rebuttal: Redwood exports model artifacts and supports model version pinning and deployment abstractions; customers can run compatible runtime in Private deployments. Pricing models include an exit assistance clause in enterprise contracts.

3) "Security/Compliance risk."
   - Rebuttal: Provide the security FAQ (below), private control plane design options, and SOC/ISO evidence during procurement.

Pitch deck one-page outline (for buy-committee meeting)

1) TL;DR: what we deliver (mission aligned with buyer outcome)
2) Architecture snapshot: hosted / dedicated / private options (one-slide diagram)
3) Economics: sample pricing scenarios tailored to buyer’s token mix (see Pricing guidance)
4) Reliability & SLOs: Downtime risk mitigation and canary + fallback strategies
5) Security & compliance summary (HSM/KMS, VPC, audit logs)
6) Pilot plan & success metrics (4–8 week pilot, acceptance criteria)

Pricing guidance (concise scenarios)

Note: pricing below is illustrative. Always generate a tailored scenario with the pricing calculator.

- Small pilot (POC): 100M tokens/month, hosted API, standard model catalog -> estimate: $X/month (include free credits and first-month discounted compute).
- Platform pilot (Dedicated small pool): 3–5 reserved GPUs, predictable throughput, 99.95% SLA -> commit-based monthly pricing with ramp credits.
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem): up-front platform license + monthly support and optional installation services.

Pricing levers to highlight to buyers:

- Batching and cache settings (can reduce per-token cost by 20–60% depending on workload)
- Quantization profile recommendations (mix of 4-bit/8-bit)
- Routing by cost/latency region to keep unit economics favorable

Case study snapshot (compact, customer-ready)

Title: FinTech alerts engine — cut inference cost and stabilized latency

- Customer profile: Series B fintech, compliance requirements, multi-region users
- Problem: Expensive per-query cost on open-source self-host setup; latency spikes during peak hours.
- Solution: Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling + KV caching, canary model rollouts, and routing by region.
- Results: 2.8x reduction in per-token cost, 40% reduction in 95th percentile latency, deployment within 6 weeks; business metric: 18% increase in fraud detection throughput within SLA windows.

Security FAQ for procurement (short answers)

Q: Can you run the control plane in our VPC?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports a private control plane that runs in the customer VPC with optional air-gapped on-prem packages for regulated workloads.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes — both cloud KMS and HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted API supports envelope encryption and per-customer keying in enterprise plans.

Q: Where is customer data logged and how long is it retained?
A: Audit logs are stored in the customer’s logging account for Private Deployments. Hosted audit logs are stored per contract terms; default retention is 90 days and can be extended via add-on.

Q: Do you provide SOC/ISO evidence?
A: Yes — SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations are available under NDA. We also provide penetration test reports and third-party assessments on request.

Q: What are your encryption practices in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. Keys are managed per customer preference (Redwood-managed or customer-managed).

Acceptance criteria for pilot (recommended)

1) Latency: p95 < 350ms for the defined request mix (or other buyer SLO).
2) Cost: per-token unit economics within 10% of modeled scenario during steady-state.
3) Stability: No more than 1 substantive incident affecting availability during pilot window.
4) Security: Pass a baseline security checklist (VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log verification).

Operational handoffs and ownership

- Sales engineering: design pilot and run pre-demo benchmarks (owner: SE).
- Customer success: onboarding and runbook transfer at pilot start (owner: CSM).
- Eng SRE: escalation path for incidents during pilot (owner: eng-sre team).

Attachments and artifacts to include in RFP packet

- One-page architecture diagram (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Short benchmark excerpt (p95, throughput numbers) with test harness details (model name, sequence length distribution)
- Pricing scenario worksheet (CSV attachment)
- Security evidence index (SOC/ISO docs, penetration test summary)

Appendix: benchmark snippet (example)

Command used:
```
# Example benchmark CLI
redwood-bench --model rdx-2.1 --payload-size 32 --concurrency 8 --duration 300 --region us-west-2
```
Results (excerpt):
- p50: 45ms per token
- p95: 290ms per token
- throughput: 1200 tokens/sec per GPU (continuous)

How to use this doc

- For a first meeting with a buy-committee, attach the executive summary, price scenario, brief case study, and the security FAQ.
- For RFP responses, include the appendix artifacts and the benchmark snippet.
- For in-depth technical review, schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with the platform architect and prepare a Private deployment reference diagram tailored to the customer network.
